problem.text: The README used deeper heading levels and an 800-wide quantization preview; the evaluation page's HumanEval image lacked the direct image link already provided for other plots.

reasoning.text: The change adjusts documentation hierarchy and image presentation rather than quantization or evaluation logic.

impact.text: HumanEval gains a clickable link to its PNG, while the README retains its link from the preview to the detailed EXL3 documentation.

limitations: No documentation renderer or browser was exercised; actual layout and target="_blank" handling remain renderer-dependent. Scalar computation would not meaningfully validate these markup changes.

claims.text: README major sections move from level-three to level-two headings; Installation, Conversion and Examples move from level four to level three, preserving their subordinate relationship to How to.

Both documents replace centered figure elements carrying class="image" with centered div elements. This retains the explicit alignment attribute but removes figure semantics and the image class hook; the resulting visual effect depends on renderer styling.

The README preview's width attribute changes from 800 to 640. The detailed comparison plots retain width 400, and HumanEval retains width 800; these are image presentation dimensions, not benchmark parameters.

HumanEval's image is wrapped in an anchor pointing to humaneval.png with target="_blank", matching the existing direct-image navigation pattern of the paired bitrate and VRAM plots. The README preview instead continues to navigate to doc/exl3.md.

annotation.summary: Adjusts README heading hierarchy, standardizes centered plot wrappers, shrinks the README preview and adds direct-image navigation for HumanEval.
